 Versus  Land Acquisition Collector and another ..Respondents -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Coram :-
Justice Jyotsna Rewal Dua, Judge Whether approved for reporting?1

__ For the Appellant : Mr. Rajiv Rai, Advocate For the Respondents : Mr. Y.P.S. Dhaulta and Mr. Rupinder Singh, Additional Advocates General, with r Ms. Seema Sharma and Mr. Sumit Sharma, Deputy Advocates General, for respondent No. 1.
Mr. C.N. Singh, Advocate, for respondent No.2.
In question is the award passed by learned District Judge on 31.10.2011 dismissing Land Reference Petition instituted by the appellant.
2. Land, in all measuring 169-15-04 bigha at village Tatapani, Tehsil Karsog, District Mandi was acquired by respondent No. 2 for construction of Kol Dam Hydropower Project.
Appellant's lands were also part of the land acquired for the project.

The Land Acquisition Collector (LAC) passed Paras Ram vs Land Acquisition Collector And Another on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152836677/
1 award No. 79/2008 on 08.03.2008.
Several reference petitions originated from this award, including Reference Petition No. 37 of 2009 instituted by the present appellant.
Vide impugned award, dated 31.10.2011, learned Reference Court/District Judge Mandi dismissed the petition.

entities.text: Paras Ram vs Land Acquisition Collector And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Another bunch of Reference Petitions arising out of same award passed by the LAC with lead case .

Reference Petition No. 28 of 2010 was decided and allowed by the learned Reference Court on 13.12.2013 as under :-
"29.

In view of my aforesaid discussion, reference petitions are allowed with costs and the reference petitioners are held entitled to enhanced compensation at the rate of Rs. 6,41,032/- per bigha in respect of acquired land and 45% in respect of the market value assessed by the Collector.
However, it is ordered that the reference petitioners shall be entitled to compensation as per their shares in the acquired land recorded in revenue record.

30. Further, the reference petitioners are also held entitled to the following reliefs :-
(a) the petitioners shall also be entitled to solatium @ 30% on the amount as stated aforesaid,
(b) the reference petitioners shall also be entitled for additional compensation @ 12%
per annum under Section 23(1-A) of the Act w.e.f. 27.02.2005 the date of publication of notification till the date of award of the Collector, i.e. 08.03.2008 and

(c) the reference petitioners shall also be entitled to interest under Section 28 of the Act on the amount assessed under sub-section (1) of Section 23 of the Act, the additional compensation worked out under sub-section (1-A) of Section 23 of the Act,
plus, solatium awarded under sub-section 23 of the Act, at the rate of 9% per annum on the value assessed from the date of award and thereafter @ 15% per annum till the date of payment/deposit of the amount of compensation in accordance with Section 34 of the Act."
Aggrieved against dismissal of his reference petition vide award dated 31.10.2011, the appellant has instituted present appeal.

3. Heard learned counsel on both sides and considered the case record.
4(i) It is not in dispute
that Reference Petition No. 28 of 2010 , decided by learned Reference Court/District Judge Mandi on 13.12.2013 also pertained to award No. 79 of 2008, announced by the LAC on .

Paras Ram vs Land Acquisition Collector And Another on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152836677/
2 08.03.2008.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this award, the Reference Court re-determined the market value of the entire acquired land by awarding Rs. 6,41,032/- per bigha irrespective of nature of land (highest rate awarded by the LAC with respect to the best quality of land).
The Reference Court did not enhance any amount other than uniformly applying the said rate with respect to the entire land acquired for the public purpose i.e. construction of Kol Dam.
The appellant/claimant has relied upon the award dated 13.12.2013 for claiming the market value of his acquired land @ 6,41,032/- per bigha.
In RFA No. 425 of 2012 (NTPC Ltd. Kol Dam Vs. Kuldeep and others) decided on 15.12.2016, this Court affirmed the determination of market value of entire acquired land @ 6,41,032/- per bigha.

entities.text: RFA No. 425 of 2012 (NTPC Ltd. Kol Dam Vs. Kuldeep and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The cross objections preferred by the claimants therein were also dismissed.

Inter alia, it was also held that "learned counsel for the parties contend that decision rendered in present appeal would automatically apply to the other connected matters which are pending before this Court".
It is an admitted position that present proceedings also arise from award No. 79 of 2008 passed by LAC on 08.03.2008.

Therefore, the market value of the land as determined by learned Reference Court in Reference Petition No. 8 of 2009, 28 of 2010 and as affirmed in RFA No. 425 of 2012 would apply to the instant case as well.

It may also be noticed that in the other similar cases arising out of same award, i.e. Award No. 79 of 2008, passed by LAC on 08.03.2008 were also disposed of in terms of judgment dated 15.12.2016 passed in RFA No. 425 of 2012 .

(NTPC Ltd. Kol Dam Vs. Kuldeep and others).Some of these matters are RFA No. 115 of 2013 (NTPC Ltd. Kol Dam Vs. Balak Ram), RFA No.113 of 2013 (NTPC Ltd. Kol Dam Vs. Banti Devi and others)
and RFA No. 152 of 2015 (Keshav Ram Vs. LAC Kol Dam) alongwith other connected matters.
4(ii) A further argument has been put forth by learned counsel for the appellant-claimant that the appellant is entitled for adequate compensation on account of structure existing over the land in question.
Issue No. 2 before the learned Reference Court was "Whether the market value of the structure assessed by the Collector is not adequate, if so, what is the market value of the structure ? OPP."
Finding on above issue was recorded by the learned Reference Court as under :-
"14.

sentences.text: Onus to prove this issue is on the petitioners.
No evidence has been led to show that what was the description of the houses which were allegedly acquired by the respondents.

In the absence of any evidence showing the exact value of the house, it is very difficult for this court to hold that inadequate compensation for the houses/superstructures was awarded to the petitioners.
This issue is accordingly decided in the negative."

During hearing of the appeal, learned counsel for the appellant could not refer to any evidence available on record to substantiate the plea that adequate compensation was not given to the Paras Ram vs Land Acquisition Collector And Another on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152836677/
3 appellant for the super- structure.

sentences.text:
Reliance was placed upon award dated 13.09.2013 passed by the learned Reference Court/District Judge, Mandi in another Reference Petition bearing No. 31 of 2009 (Keshav Ram Vs.
N.T.P.C.) to contend .
that in this award, compensation was enhanced in respect of house of the claimant (therein).
On the same analogy, prayer was made for awarding compensation in respect of structure said to be existing over the land in question.
As already noticed above, there is no evidence on record to substantiate the factual contention urged by the appellant.

Additionally, the award passed in Reference Petition No. 31 of 2009 became subject matter of appeal being RFA No. 152 of 2015, which was decided on 09.08.2018 on the lines of decision in Kuldeep's case (supra), holding as under :-
"3.

It is not in dispute that appeal arising out of similarly situated claimants, as also very same acquisition proceedings, arising out of very same notifications under Sections 4 and 11 of the Act, stands decided by this Court vide judgment dated 15.12.2016, passed in RFA No. 425 of 2012, titled as NTPC Ltd. Kol Dam Vs. Kuldeep & others.

entities.text: NTPC Ltd. Kol Dam Vs. Kuldeep & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The rpesent appeals are squarely covered by the said decision, for the issue involved is identical.
This fact is not disputed.
As such, the present appeals stand dispose dof in terms of the said judgment.
Directions issued in Kuldeep (supra) shall mutatis mutandis apply to the instant cases also.
Pending application(s), if any, also stand disposed of accordingly.
In view of above, the claim that adequate compensation was not paid in respect of structure over the acquired land cannot be accepted.

5. In light of above discussion, the ultimate analysis is that present appeal is squarely covered by the judgment dated 15.12.2016 passed in RFA No 425 of 2012 (NTPC Ltd.
Kol Dam Vs. Kuldip).
